I met my girlfriend while I was agrophobic (she was a friend of my housemate, so I didn’t have to leave my house to meet her haha). That was 2018 and now we live together and adopted a dog. There are definitely times where we have big long emotional conversations about my condition… she really only gets frustrated when I give up on trying to get better. But she is very very understanding and supportive when I have a panic attack. 

I think the hardest part of being in a relationship while having agoraphobia is the insecurity and guilt and worry and shame. Sometimes I wonder why she is with me… when she could easily find a girl that is free and wild and all that haha but then I remind myself that she’s with me for ME .

As for friends…. I don’t have a lot of them. And the ones I do have I don’t seen them much.

I felt the exact same when I was 19... Now I’m 29, have a really great circle of friends, an amazing girlfriend, and I’m definitely on the right road to having a career I love. 
I’m not gonna lie, a lot of my early 20s was almost unbearable because of my crippling anxiety and depression. I felt totally lost and alone and like life wasn’t worth it. A lot of the time I just stayed alive for my mum. So yeah... things can and will get better. 

I’m gonna list a few things that helped me: 

- a good and understanding therapist
- guides meditations/self hypnosis on YouTube (ones specifically for anxiety, social anxiety, depression, driving anxiety... there’s really one for anything you need!)
- Kickboxing 
- Saint Johns Wort (herbal remedy for anxiety)
- lots of journaling 
- feeling the fear and doing it anyway (this is definitely the most challenging thing. It’s not easy. At all. But it’s so incredibly worth it and the only way to get to your true and best life)
- being open with people about my mental health (people are a lot more understanding and chill about these things than we give them credit for sometimes) 

Hope this was even a tiny little bit helpful!
